q: In what order should you read an EXPLAIN plan?
options: From the inside out: go to the deepest nodes and walk up
Top line first, then down
Bottom line only
Alphabetically by node name
why: The first line of a plan is the last step.

q: The plan says `rows=10` (the guess) but `actual rows=500000`. What is the first thing to try?
options: Add more RAM
Run `ANALYZE` on the table so the planner has fresh notes, then read the plan again
Drop all indexes on the table
Rewrite the query with a subquery
why: A guess far from the truth means old notes.

q: What does `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` do that plain `EXPLAIN` does not?
options: It makes the query faster
It only shows the cost in dollars
It really runs the query and shows real times and row counts
It rebuilds the table statistics only
why: Plain EXPLAIN is the map (a guess). ANALYZE adds the dashcam (the truth). Careful: it really runs an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE too.

q: Is a Seq Scan always bad?
options: Yes, always add an index
Yes, it means the table is corrupt
No, but only on tables with fewer than 10 rows
No. It is fine when it keeps most of what it reads. It is bad when it throws away almost everything
why: A Seq Scan that throws away 99.9% of rows is the one to fix.

q: What are the steps of the slow query workflow?
options: Find it, explain it, find the hot node, fix it, measure again
Add an index, add another index, restart Postgres
Guess, change, deploy
VACUUM FULL, then ANALYZE, then done
why: Always measure again after the fix. Without that you do not know it worked.
